issues.description: SealSaloon constructor signature is inconsistent: the problem statement/UML require a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts a saloon name, but the template usage and reference solution provide and expect a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This leaves students unsure whether to implement SealSaloon() or SealSaloon(String) and whether a name field/getter is required.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the constructor requirement consistent across all artifacts. Two viable remedies:
1) Prefer change in problem statement/UML: update the UML and text to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (remove text about passing a saloon name), keeping the template and solution as-is.
OR
2) Prefer change in template & solution: implement SealSaloon(String name) in both template and solution, add a private final String name field initialized from the constructor, and provide a public getter getName(). Ensure the default orders initialization remains (e.g., this.orders = new Meal[]{};) and preserve static stock behavior. Update Main and any examples to call new SealSaloon("name").

issues.description: Constructor naming and presence mismatch for the SealSaloon class: the problem statement (UML and text) requires a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts a saloon name and implies a corresponding name field/getter, whereas the provided code (both the template usage in Main.java and the reference solution) use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() and do not declare a saloon name. This inconsistency can confuse students: the problem calls the constructor SealSaloon(String) and asks for a saloon name parameter, but the template instantiates new SealSaloon() (no args) and the solution implements public SealSaloon() with no name field or getter, so students may be unsure whether to implement a String parameter constructor, add a name field/getter, or leave the no-arg constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Preferred fix: implement SealSaloon(String name) in the code (add a private final String name field, set it in the constructor, and add a getName() getter), update the no-arg constructor usages in Main (or provide a convenience no-arg constructor delegating to the String constructor), and keep the static stock semantics as specified. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and remove the saloon name requirement—ensure all artifacts consistently document the chosen API.
